{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is neutral or negative (sentiment ≤ 0.00) to correct for overconfidence in upward moves.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility in early periods (e.g., first 5 days) when price is trending downward — model tends to overreact.",
    "When true outcome spikes sharply (e.g., >10% from prior day), reduce forecast overshoot by 15–20% to avoid overcorrection.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment is positive.",
    "In late periods (e.g., last 5 days of forecast), increase downward bias if sentiment is neutral — model tends to overestimate recovery.",
    "If sentiment is positive (≥0.25), allow forecast to rise slightly above true outcome, but cap at +10% to avoid overestimating bullish momentum.",
    "When true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid persistent overestimation.",
    "In high volatility periods (e.g., 3+ consecutive days with >5% price swings), apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast noise."
  ]
}
